title: India Marks 12th National Handloom Day With Awards, Exhibition at Rashtrapati Bhavan
excerpt: President Droupadi Murmu presides over celebrations honoring India's handloom weavers as PM Modi renews his 'Vocal for Local' call for the sector that supports 3.5 million livelihoods.
body:
• India celebrated the 12th National Handloom Day on August 7, 2026, with a national function at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre in New Delhi, presided over by President Droupadi Murmu
  • Twenty-two awards — including 3 Sant Kabir Handloom Awards and 19 National Handloom Awards — were conferred on outstanding weavers, alongside the release of four commemorative postage stamps
  • The handloom sector supports over 3.5 million livelihoods in India, with women making up more than 70% of the workforce

National Function at Rashtrapati Bhavan

India observed the 12th National Handloom Day on August 7, 2026, with the main celebration held at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre in New Delhi. President Droupadi Murmu served as the chief guest, joined by Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh, Minister of State for Textiles Pabitra Margherita, and senior officials including Secretary (Textiles) Neelam Shami Rao and Development Commissioner (Handlooms) Dr. M. Beena, according to the Ministry of Textiles.

The event brought together more than 1,000 weavers from across the country, alongside designers, industry representatives, exporters, and members of Parliament.

Awards and New Publications

A total of 22 awards were presented during the ceremony. Three weavers received the prestigious Sant Kabir Handloom Awards, while 19 received National Handloom Awards, recognizing outstanding craftsmanship, innovation, and contributions to preserving India's handloom traditions, the Ministry of Textiles announced.

The function also saw the release of four commemorative postage stamps celebrating India's handloom weaving heritage and two new publications — "Earth. Root. Thread — Aal Dyed Handloom Textiles of Central India" and the Handloom Awards Book 2025. An exhibition of award-winning handloom products was organized alongside live demonstrations of traditional Kani weaving and wall hanging weaving.

"Greetings on National Handloom Day! We take immense pride in the rich heritage and vibrant tradition of handlooms across our nation. We also cherish the efforts of our artisans and reiterate our commitment to be 'Vocal for Local.'"

— PM Narendra Modi, via social media platform X

The Swadeshi Movement Connection

National Handloom Day is observed annually on August 7 to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched on this date in 1905, which encouraged the use of domestically produced goods over British imports. The first National Handloom Day was inaugurated by PM Modi on August 7, 2015, at the Centenary Hall of Madras University in Chennai.

The day was chosen to honor the spirit of the movement that connected India's weavers with the broader independence struggle. PM Modi has consistently championed the handloom sector, recently using his Mann Ki Baat radio address on July 26 to call on citizens to support the 'Vocal for Local' campaign ahead of the celebrations.

A Sector Supporting Millions

India's handloom sector remains one of the country's largest sources of sustainable rural employment, supporting the livelihoods of more than 35 lakh (3.5 million) people, with women constituting over 70% of the workforce, according to government data. The sector accounts for approximately 15% of India's total cloth production, and about 95% of the world's hand-woven fabric comes from India.

The 'Weaves of India' festival, organized by the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms) at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium on Janpath, New Delhi, showcased 116 heritage weaves from states including Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir, and Tripura. The festival ran from July 24 to August 7, according to the Press Information Bureau.

Diaspora Connection

For the Indian diaspora, handloom textiles are a tangible link to regional identity and heritage. Banarasi silks, Kanchipuram sarees, and Pashmina shawls are staples at weddings, festivals, and cultural events in NRI communities worldwide, making the sector's health a matter of cultural significance beyond India's borders.

What's Next

Additional events around National Handloom Day include designer conclaves and exhibitions at Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology campuses. The government has signaled continued investment in the sector, positioning handloom as both a cultural asset and an engine of sustainable, women-led employment growth.
